title: Varna 7. The Meeting of Sri Jagadisha with Sri Mahaprabhu
html:
Jagadisha lives in Navadvipa next to Jagannatha Mishra and prays to Krishna to descend; the Lord's appearance in Shachi's house; Duhkhini nurses the infant Nimai; Jagadisha and Hiranya Bhagavata keep Ekadashi to call Krishna down; the weeping Nimai demands their offering to Vishnu; on another Ekadashi the Lord eats the offering during Jagadisha's puja and reveals Himself to him; Duhkhini sees the four-armed form; the Lord calls them His associates from Dvapara; Jagadisha dances in prema; the kirtanas at Srivasa's house and the subduing of the Kazi; with the Lord's permission Jagadisha leaves Duhkhini with Mahesha and sets out for Nilachala; the author's signature

The seventh varna

1Glory, glory to Jagadisha, glory to the ocean of mercy!
You are the message of deliverance for the living beings, the friend of the lowly.

2Thus Prabhu Jagadisha in Navadvipa
took up residence near Jagannatha Mishra.1

3The wife of Mishra Thakura is Shachi Thakurani;
Duhkhini became very dear to her.

4Thus Jagadisha, living in that place,
began to worship Krishna with body, words and mind.

5The Prabhu worships Krishna with joy in his heart;
Srimati Duhkhini serves him.

6The mind of Duhkhini Devi is wholly devoted to Krishna;
seeing [this], Prabhu Jagadisha is glad at heart.

7Thus Jagadisha lives in Nadia;
seeing people turned away from Sri Krishna, he suffers.

8Becoming compassionate towards all those living beings,
he ponders a means: how will they be saved?

9Jagadisha says: "Krishna, descend
and deliver all these people who are turned away [from You].

10Let all worship Your lotus feet —
this is my desire in body, mind and words."

11Thus Jagadisha performs worship
and prays for the deliverance of the living beings.

12In this way many days passed,
and Sri Jagadisha's desire was fulfilled.

13To fulfil the desire of His devotee, the merciful Lord
Krishnachandra rose in Shachi's house.

14Covering His black complexion, He became golden:
in that complexion He took on [the lustre of] jambunada gold.2

15The pastimes of that Lord are countless and boundless;
they are [described] in detail in the Chaitanya-charitamrita.

16I have no power to describe them;
forgive me [this] offence, devotees of Gaura.

17In Shachi's house Chaitanya Gosani descended;
His father gave Him the name Nimai.

18Nimai's mother and Thakurani Duhkhini
are very happy on seeing each other.3

19The love between them is like that of two sisters born of one mother:
whoever does not know [them] thinks just that.

20Shachi's son grew up supremely beautiful;
seeing [Him], Duhkhini rejoices boundlessly at heart.

21Shachi Devi entrusted her son to Duhkhini
and with great affection began to say to her:

22"This is my son, beautiful Nimai;
always keep Him close to you."

23Hearing this from Shachi's holy lips, [Duhkhini] Devi
in supreme bliss took Nimai on her lap.

24And so Duhkhini Devi, taking Nimai,
fondles and rears [Him], happy at heart.

25Thus, her mind filled with tenderness for Nimai,
she rears Him, thinking Him an ordinary child.

26[There was] a great-minded [brahmana] named Hiranya Bhagavata,
a supreme devotee of Krishna, living in Navadvipa.

27With him Jagadisha, in the joy of prema,
constantly remains in talks about Krishna.

28The two have one mind and one and the same bhajana;
both with love perform the worship of Sri Krishna.

29For the sake of worldly pleasures the world is full of craving;
bewildered by maya, the living beings do not worship Krishna.

30If they are admonished, no one listens;
to the one who admonishes they speak harsh words.

31Thus, deluded by Vishnu's maya,
all the living beings remain, having forgotten Krishna.

32For their sake both ponder:
in what way will they all be delivered?

33"If Krishna comes and descends,
then the deliverance of all these living beings will take place.

34Sri Krishna will come and deliver the living beings —
then indeed all these living beings will be delivered."

35"We will bring Sri Krishna" — such is the desire of both;
they consider how [this] desire may be fulfilled.

36Pondering and pondering, [they] remembered a verse,
and, reflecting on that verse, they found joy.

Tatha hi, in the Sri Brihan-naradiya Purana:

37The vow called Ekadashi bestows the fruit of all desires;
brahmanas must keep it by all means — [it] is the cause of Vishnu's pleasure.4

38Whoever among men keeps this vow of Ekadashi,
all his desires are fulfilled.

39[It is] the duty of a brahmana, for the sake of Vishnu's pleasure;
from this all desires are fulfilled.

40Having considered thus, both rejoiced
and with great bliss began [to keep] the vow of Ekadashi.

41With devotion both keep the vow of Ekadashi;
its procedure is according to the shastras.

Tatha hi, in the Sri Vishnu Purana:

42[Keeping] the Ekadashi of both fortnights, without food, concentrated,
having bathed according to the rules, in clean clothes, with senses controlled,

43having worshipped Vishnu according to the rules with faith, deeply concentrated —
with flowers, fragrances, and likewise incense, lamps, excellent naivedya,

44with many kinds of gifts, japa, homa and circumambulations,
with various hymns, with charming dance, song and music,

45with prostrations like a rod, and likewise with excellent cries of "jaya" —
having thus worshipped [Him] according to the rules, let him keep vigil at night;

46let one devoted to Vishnu tell narrations or sing songs —
[such] a man reaches the supreme abode of Vishnu: of this there is no doubt.5

47In this way both keep the vow of Ekadashi
and worship Krishna according to the rules of the shastras.

48With bows and praises both pray:
"Krishna, fulfil the desire of us both.

49O Lord, come Yourself, descend,
and deliver the living beings bewildered by maya.

50Let all give up being pashandas and become Vaishnavas;
let all know, O Lord, Your glory.

51Let the living beings worship no one but You;
become the wealth and life of all the living beings.

52O Lord, deliver the living beings, coming Yourself;
make the living beings happy by giving [them] bhakti for Yourself.

53This, O Lord, is the desire of us both:
O Lord, deliver all the living beings."

54Having prayed thus to the feet of Sri Krishna,
both keep the vow of Ekadashi with joy in their hearts.

55Seeing the firmness of both in the vow, Gaura Raya,
the Lord, seeks a means to meet the two.

56One day Mahaprabhu is weeping;
His mother comforts [Him], but He will not be calmed.

57Before His father and mother He shows wilfulness:
the Lord asks for just what cannot be had.

58Whatever the Lord asks for, His father and mother give;
and still Mahaprabhu weeps.

59For this there is only one remedy:
on hearing the name of Hari, the Lord weeps no more.

60To comfort the Lord, all the men and women
loudly sing "Hare Krishna, Hare Rama".

61And still Mahaprabhu does not calm down;
He tells no reason, but only weeps.

62Shachi Devi says: "Child, why are You crying?"
The Lord says: "A fit has come upon Me just now.6

63All of you, find out [what it is] and treat it;
then, calmed down, I will play."

64Hearing this, everyone treats [Him],
and still Mahaprabhu weeps.

65Mishra says: "Child Vishvambhara, what do You want?
That very thing I will give, child — stop crying."

66The Lord says: "If you want to make Me well,
then go quickly to the house of two brahmanas.

67Jagadisha Pandita [and] Hiranya Bhagavata —
the two brahmanas are keeping the vow of Ekadashi today.

68They have prepared naivedya to worship Vishnu;
if I get to eat it, I will cry no more."

69Hearing these words from the boy's mouth,
Mishra's wife laments greatly.7

70Hearing [of this], those two brahmanas came quickly,
brought Vishnu's naivedya and placed it before the Lord.

71Having eaten it, Mahaprabhu became calm;
that this was Sri Krishna Himself, they did not know.

72Then the Lord thought in His heart:
"I will make Myself known to Jagadisha.8

73Again on an Ekadashi day I will eat the naivedya,
and on that day I will let him see Me."

74In this way some days passed,
and then Mahaprabhu met Jagadisha.

75On another Ekadashi day the Lord considered:
"Now Jagadisha has begun the worship of Krishna.

76At this time I shall go there" —
having considered [thus], Mahaprabhu set out at once.

77Arriving, He saw Jagadisha Pandita:
in the worship of Krishna he had forgotten the outer world.

78Many articles of naivedya of various kinds —
fruits, roots, sweets and the like — beyond counting.

79Fixing his mind on Krishna, Jagadisha offers [them];
seeing [this], Mahaprabhu became filled with supreme bliss.

80Receiving the devotee's articles, Sri Gauranga Raya joyfully
displayed there something of a child's restlessness:

81as if unknowingly, He ate a little of the naivedya.
At that moment the Pandita's meditation was broken.

82Jagadisha says: "What have You done, Nimai?
You have eaten the naivedya — the worship of Vishnu has not been done."

83The Lord says: "Jagadisha, listen to [My] words:
come and worship My feet as [the feet of] Krishna."

84Jagadisha sees that this son of Shachi
is Sri Krishna Himself — of this there is no doubt.

85Prostrating on the ground with all eight limbs, he bows down
and again and again offers praises with joined palms.

86The Lord says: "You are an old brahmana, a venerable man;
it is not fitting for you to bow to Me.

87You are an aged pandita, all-knowing,
and by bowing to Me you bring misfortune on Me."

88Jagadisha says: "O Lord, deceive me no more:
I have seen with my own eyes the marks on Your feet."

Tatha hi:

89The lotus feet which Brahma and the others, constantly meditating, have not attained — You, O wondrous One, I have seen with my own eyes by my good fortune.

90Brahma, Bhava and the other gods, always absorbed in meditation,
constantly long to attain those feet.

91By the good fortune of many births, one after another,
today I have seen that pair of feet with my own eyes.

92For so many days I, wretched one, did not recognize [You];
today my body has become fruitful.

93Since You, O Lord, have shown mercy to a low sinner,
mercifully give me the shade of Your feet upon my head.

94To Your devotee You have given Your pair of feet;
now You will never be able to trick [him]."

95Thus Jagadisha offers various praises
and says: "Forgive me [my] offence."

96At that time Duhkhini Devi came there,
and, coming, she saw the holy feet of Mahaprabhu.

97On the soles shine the marks of the flag, the thunderbolt and the elephant goad;
in the four arms are the conch, disc, club and lotus.

98On the chest a garland of forest flowers, on the hips a dhara;
the forehead framed by curls, above the form a chuda.9

99Seeing such beauty, Duhkhini fainted;
after a moment she came to her senses.

100With tears in her eyes the Devi says to the Lord:
"At last, O Lord, You have become kind to me.

101At last You have made my birth fruitful:
forgiving my offence, You have let me see You.

102I reared [You], thinking You an ordinary child;
forgive me this offence, Narayana.

103I am a woman, ignorant, I have no strength at all;
O Lord, give [me] firm bhakti for Your lotus feet."

104Thus Duhkhini Devi, offering many praises,
bowed down, [falling] like a rod, holding the Lord's feet.

105Jagadisha [and] Duhkhini bowed to the Lord's feet;
mercifully the Lord began to speak to them both:

106"You two were formerly My associates,
and now you have taken birth as devotees.

107In the same way the associates [of My lila in] Dvapara
have been born in the form of devotees in various places.

108I have met with you before all the others,
and later I will meet with all the devotees.10

109All together we shall practise the bhagavata-dharma
and spread the sankirtana of the name of Hari.

110In the age of Kali the living beings are intoxicated with worldly things;
by giving the name of Hari, I will deliver them all."

111Hearing Gauranga's words, Pandita Thakura
found abundant bliss in his mind.

112Intoxicated with prema, Jagadisha began to dance;
then Mahaprabhu calmed him.

113In this way Jagadisha met the Lord
and together with his wife began to serve His feet.

114Listen with faith, all you devotees,
[to the account of] Jagadisha's meeting with Mahaprabhu.

115After some time the Lord, with His devotees,
performs kirtana filled with supreme bliss.

116Gathering at night in the house of Srivasa Pandita,
all cry "Hari, Hari!", clapping their hands.

117Then Mahaprabhu manifested the sankirtana;
because of it there was a great clash with the Kazi.

118Having crushed the Kazi, the Lord performs sankirtana
and joyfully enjoys His pastimes with His circle of devotees.11

119For the deliverance of the pashandas the Lord Gaurahari
ponders in His mind day and night.

120He considered in His mind the means for this;
that news Jagadisha came to know in his heart:

121the Lord, leaving Navadvipa and becoming a sannyasi,
will live at Jagannatha's together with the devotees.

122Knowing [this], Jagadisha conceived a desire in his mind:
"I will manifest the service of Sri Jagannatha.12

123Leaving Navadvipa, I will live in another place.
How shall I obtain Gauranga's command for this?"

124Gaura, the wish-fulfilling tree for the desires of His devotees, the jewel of virtues, called Jagadisha and Himself gave the command.

125The Lord says: "Jagadisha, listen to [My] words:
go — your wish will be fulfilled."

126Receiving the command, Jagadisha became very happy;
he called Mahesha Pandita and began to speak:

127"I will go to Niladri to see Jagannatha;
I leave Duhkhini in your house."13

128Having thus reassured his own brother,
he set out for Nilachala with joy in his heart.

129Whoever hears this account with faith
obtains Chaitanya's feet by Jagadisha's mercy.

130Placing hope in the feet of Prabhu Bhagavatananda,
Ananda Dasa tells of Jagadisha's pastimes.

Thus in the Charitra-vijaya of Sri Jagadisha Pandita ends the seventh varna, called "The Meeting of Sri Jagadisha with Sri Mahaprabhu".

Notes

  1. See varna 6, note 9. Here the merging of the two Jagadishas shows openly: Jagadisha and Duhkhini live next to Jagannatha Mishra's family even before the Lord's appearance, and Duhkhini nurses Nimai (21–25); further on, Jagadisha is paired with Hiranya Bhagavata (Hiranya Pandita of Navadvipa, 26–28), and the weeping Nimai demands their Ekadashi offering to Vishnu (55–71) — the episode of Jagadisha and Hiranya (GGD 192) in the CB (Adi 6) and the CC (Adi 14). Cf. also 86–87, where Jagadisha is "an old brahmana", "an aged pandita".
  2. The edition reads «বর্ণনে ধৃত» (varṇane dhṛta); taken as «বর্ণে ধৃত» (varṇe dhṛta), "in that complexion took on". Jambunada is the finest gold (named after the river Jambu). Cf. Bhagavata 11.5.32 (kṛṣṇa-varṇaṁ tviṣākṛṣṇam) and CC Adi 4: Krishna, taking on Radha's lustre and mood, descends as golden Gaura.
  3. «ঠাকুরাণী দুঃখী» (ṭhākurāṇī duḥkhī) — a short form of the name Duhkhini (for the metre).
  4. The edition reads «বিষ্ণুপ্রীতেন কারনং» (viṣṇu-prītena kāraṇaṁ); taken as viṣṇu-prīti-kāraṇam, "the cause of Vishnu's pleasure".
  5. The five verses (42–46) form one sentence. "The Ekadashi of both fortnights" (ekādaśyām ubhau pakṣau) — the Ekadashi of the bright and of the dark half of the lunar month. Naivedya — food offered to the Deity.
  6. «বাই» (bāi, from Skt. vāyu, "wind") — in popular belief, a disorder of the "wind" in the body: a fit, a whim.
  7. The edition reads «বহুত কারনে খেদ» (bahuta kārane kheda); taken as «বহুত করেন খেদ» (bahuta karena kheda), "laments greatly"; possibly also "laments for many reasons".
  8. The second episode — the Lord eats the offering during Jagadisha's puja and reveals Himself to him (72–113) — is not in the CB or the CC: they tell only of the first, when the offering of Jagadisha and Hiranya is brought to the weeping Nimai (CB Adi 6; CC Adi 14).
  9. Dhara (ধড়া, dhaṛā) — the loincloth of the cowherd boy Krishna; chuda (চূড়া, cūṛā) — the topknot adorned with a peacock feather. The edition reads «অলকামৃত» (alakāmṛta); taken as «অলকাবৃত» (alakāvṛta), "framed by curls"; «তনু পরি» (tanu pari) — the reading is unclear; taken as "above the form".
  10. "Before all the others" is the author's statement. In the CB the Lord begins to reveal Himself to His associates after His return from Gaya (CB Madhya 1–2).
  11. The Kazi — Chand Kazi, the ruler of Navadvipa, who forbade kirtana and was subdued by the Lord (CC Adi 17; CB Madhya 23).
  12. An anticipation of the account of Jagannatha, whom Jagadisha served at Yashoda (Jatra).
  13. Niladri, Nilachala ("the Blue Mountain") — Puri.
